sample_and_generalization_limitations: Sample Size: Only 44 validation races across two seasons (2022 and 2023) are available in the chronological walk-forward setup.
Temporal Autocorrelation: Races within a single season share aerodynamic regulations, tire compounds, and development curves; observations are not strictly independent i.i.d. draws.

Cross-Era Transferability: A statistically significant paired t-test on 2022-2023 demonstrates sample superiority, but does not mathematically guarantee generalization across future regulation transitions (e.g. 2026).
Season-Level Degrees of Freedom: Two validation seasons provide only 2 season-level units, precluding formal season-level hierarchical random-effects modeling.
reconciliation_synthesis.definitive_evidence_verdict: Candidate w=0.20 unequivocally retains its statistically significant advantage over the empirical grid baseline across all three calibration regimes. In the rigorous chronological OOF regime (Regime 2), w=0.20 achieves Delta = -0.2273 (nominal p = 3.99e-04, Holm-adjusted p = 4.39e-03), surviving both Bonferroni and Holm corrections. In the natural uncalibrated regime (Regime 3), w=0.20 achieves Delta = -0.2506 (nominal p = 2.45e-04, Holm-adjusted p = 2.70e-03). The observed advantage is therefore mathematically confirmed to be independent of temperature scaling choices.
